summary: Creates an IANA registry for the cost modes supported by the ALTO protocol and relaxes a constraint the ALTO specification placed on allowed cost mode values. It updates RFC 7285. It is a standards-track specification.

eli5.summary: ALTO can say how costly a path is in different ways. This starts an official list of those ways so people can add new ones without clashing.

subtitle: A new IANA registry for the ways ALTO can say how its cost values should be read.

tldr.problem: The ALTO base specification allowed only two cost modes, numerical and ordinal, but some deployments need more.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 9274 relaxes the rule that limited cost modes to those two strings, sets encoding limits on mode names, and creates an IANA registry called ALTO Cost Modes.
tldr.outcome: New cost modes can now be defined and registered under IETF Review, with a private-use prefix of priv: for local ones. It updates RFC 7285.

today: RFC 9274 is a Proposed Standard from July 2022 that updates RFC 7285. No later RFC obsoletes or updates it according to the metadata.

sections.title: Why Cost Modes Needed a Registry
sections.content:
In the Application-Layer Traffic Optimization (ALTO) protocol from RFC 7285, the cost mode attribute tells a client how to interpret the costs it receives. The base specification provides for only two modes.

The numerical mode says numerical operations, such as normalization, can be performed on the returned costs. The ordinal mode says the cost values in a cost map represent a ranking relative to all other values, not actual costs.

RFC 9274 points out that additional cost modes are required for specific ALTO deployment cases, such as the Path Vector extension, then relaxes the limit on allowed modes and creates a registry to track new ones.
sections.eli5: Imagine a list that says 'how far' either in real miles or just as first, second, third. ALTO only knew those two ways, and this RFC lets people add more.

sections.title: Opening the Door to New Modes
sections.content:
The first update changes Section 6.1.2 of RFC 7285. The old text described the attribute as indicating whether costs are numerical values or ordinal rankings. The new text says two modes are defined but additional ones can be defined in the future.

The RFC strongly recommends that any future document defining a new cost mode say whether it applies to all cost metrics or only a subset. This is meant to prevent nondeterministic behavior when a mode is paired with a metric where the combination does not make sense or cannot be interpreted unambiguously.

If a definition does not say, ALTO implementations MUST be prepared to accept that cost mode for any cost metric.
sections.eli5: The rule book used to say there are only two kinds. Now it says more can be invented, and anyone inventing one should say where it can be used.

sections.title: Encoding Rules for Cost Mode Names
sections.content:
The second update changes Section 10.5 of RFC 7285. Previously a cost mode string had to be either numerical or ordinal. Now the string MUST be no more than 32 characters long.

It MUST NOT contain characters other than US-ASCII letters and digits, the hyphen-minus, the colon and the low line (underscore). Cost modes reserved for Private Use are prefixed with priv:. Any other cost mode MUST be one listed in the new registry.
sections.eli5: Names must be short and use only simple letters, digits and a few symbols, like a username with rules. Names starting with priv: are for your own private use.

sections.title: Backward Compatibility
sections.content:
Servers that support new cost modes for particular cost metrics advertise this with the capability mechanism in Section 9.2 of RFC 7285. Clients, including legacy ones, use that information to set cost constraints in requests.

If a client asks for a cost mode a server does not support, the server answers with the error code E_INVALID_FIELD_VALUE. Legacy servers do the same for any cost type other than numerical or ordinal with the routingcost metric.

The new encoding limits introduce no interoperability issue, because the cost modes currently implemented already follow them.
sections.eli5: If you ask for a kind of answer a server does not know, it politely says it cannot understand the request. Older servers already do that.

sections.title: The ALTO Cost Modes Registry
sections.content:
IANA created the ALTO Cost Modes subregistry inside the ALTO Protocol registry. The assignment policy is IETF Review.

A registration request must give four things: an Identifier (the mode name), a Description, the Intended Semantics (a reference to where the meaning is defined) and a Reference to the registering document. Identifiers starting with priv: are reserved for Private Use, and IANA added a note saying so.

The registry starts with two entries, numerical and ordinal, both pointing at Sections 6.1.2.1 and 6.1.2.2 of RFC 7285 with RFC 9274 as the reference.
sections.eli5: It is an official notebook of all allowed kinds. To add a new one, the proposal has to pass a review, and the first two are already written in.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The document says it does not introduce new concerns beyond those already discussed in Section 15 of RFC 7285. Nothing further is specified.

The change is administrative: it affects how modes are named and tracked, not how ALTO messages are protected.
sections.eli5: This only adds a list and naming rules, so there are no new safety worries beyond the ones ALTO already had.
